title: Understanding Conditional Offers: What They Require
summary: Understand conditional university offers for IB students, including total points, HL grades, subject conditions, deadlines, and final result checks.
body_markdown:
A **conditional offer** means a university will admit you only if you satisfy every requirement stated in the offer. For an IB student, this commonly includes a specified Diploma total, particular Higher Level grades, a required subject result, the full IB Diploma, and sometimes language or administrative conditions.


The conditions are cumulative. If an offer asks for **36 points with 6,6,5 at Higher Level, including 6 in Mathematics AA HL** , earning 38 points with a 5 in Mathematics does not meet the written terms. Understanding conditional offers during the September-to-November application period helps you choose realistic courses and identify the grades that matter most.


### What a conditional offer means


A conditional offer is not final admission confirmation. It becomes confirmed when the university verifies that you have met the stated conditions by the relevant deadline.


Universities use conditional offers because many IB students apply before completing their final examinations. Predicted grades help admissions teams assess likely performance, but official final results determine whether academic conditions have been met. RevisionDojo's guide to[how predicted grades affect university offers](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/predicted-grades-and-university-offers) explains the distinction.


Terminology differs internationally. Conditional offers are standard in the UK, while Canadian and Australian universities may call admission conditional or provisional. US institutions often admit students on the expectation that they complete their current programme and maintain their academic performance. In every system, read the offer letter, applicant portal, and admissions terms carefully.


### Conditions IB students commonly receive


An IB offer may contain several independent requirements.


Type of condition Example What it requires


Overall Diploma score **36 points overall** Your final Diploma total must reach 36, usually including core points unless stated otherwise.


Combined HL profile **6,6,5 at HL** Your three Higher Level grades must match or exceed this combination.


Named subject grade **6 in Chemistry HL** Chemistry HL must be at least a 6, even if your total is higher.


Required course **Mathematics AA HL** Another mathematics course or level may not satisfy the prerequisite.


Diploma status **IB Diploma awarded** Individual course results are insufficient if the full Diploma is required.


Additional condition English test, deposit, health check, or document Academic results alone may not complete admission or enrolment.


Treat the offer as a checklist joined by **and** , not **or** . A high overall total does not normally compensate automatically for a missed named-subject or HL condition.


### Decoding an IB offer


Consider this example:


> Obtain the International Baccalaureate Diploma with 38 points overall, including 6,6,6 at Higher Level and grade 6 in Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL.


The student must receive the full Diploma, earn at least **38 total points** , achieve an HL profile of at least **6,6,6** , and earn at least **6 in Mathematics AA HL** .


A result of 39 points with HL grades 7,6,5, including 5 in Mathematics AA HL, misses both the HL profile and mathematics conditions. The university could still admit the student, but the written offer has not been met.


### Entry requirements and final offers are different


Published entry requirements show the usual academic standard for a course, but they are not necessarily the exact conditions an individual applicant will receive. Universities may vary offers according to the programme, applicant context, qualifications, or admissions policy.


Meeting the published requirements also does not guarantee an offer. Competitive courses may use admissions tests, interviews, written work, references, and the wider academic record to select among qualified applicants.


Oxford, for example, states that its general IB expectations range from **38-40 points** , including core points, with 6s and 7s at Higher Level. Applicants must still check the individual course page because subject requirements vary. Your own offer wording ultimately determines what you must achieve.


### What to do during the fall application term


For **2027 entry** , completed UCAS applications have been accepted since **1 September 2026** . The deadline is **15 October 2026 at 18:00 UK time** for Oxford, Cambridge, and most medicine, dentistry, veterinary medicine, and veterinary science courses. For most other undergraduate courses, the equal consideration deadline is **13 January 2027 at 18:00 UK time** . Schools often impose earlier internal deadlines.


Before applying, create a requirements sheet for every course. Record:


- The overall IB points requirement.
- The required HL profile and named subject grades.
- Whether a subject must be taken at HL.
- Which IB Mathematics course is accepted.
- Language requirements, tests, interviews, or portfolios.
- University and school submission deadlines.


Compare requirements with predicted grades component by component. A predicted total of 39 does not make you academically suitable for a course requiring 38 if you have a predicted 5 in a subject that explicitly requires 6. The[RevisionDojo UCAS guide for IB students](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ucas-university-applications-ib-parent-guide) provides a broader application checklist.


When an offer arrives, copy its exact wording into a tracker. Include response dates, document deadlines, deposits, and instructions from the university portal. If a phrase is unclear, ask admissions a precise question in writing rather than relying on another applicant's interpretation.


### Firm and insurance choices in UCAS


Your **firm choice** is your first-choice offer. If it remains conditional and you meet its requirements, that is normally where you will study.


An **insurance choice** is a backup to a conditional firm choice. It should usually have more achievable conditions, but it must also be a course you would genuinely attend. Compare complete requirements rather than overall totals alone. An offer of 35 points with 6 in Physics HL may be riskier than 36 points with 5 in Physics HL if Physics is your weakest subject.


Check your personal response deadline in UCAS. You cannot wait for results and then freely choose between your firm and insurance places.


### How universities receive final IB results


Universities need official results, not screenshots from a candidate account. Current-session students can request transcript delivery through their DP coordinator before results are released, and an admissions centre such as UCAS can count as one destination.


For May-session students, the request should normally be arranged before **5 July** . For November-session students, it should be arranged before **16 December** . The IB's[official transcript guidance](https://ibo.org/university-admission/support-students-transition-to-higher-education/requesting-and-sending-transcripts/) explains destination limits and post-results requests.


Confirm that your coordinator has authorised the correct destination. Even successful grades cannot be processed promptly if the university does not receive the official result.


### What happens if you miss a condition


Missing a condition means your place is not automatically confirmed, but it does not always mean rejection. The university may admit you, leave the decision pending, offer an alternative course, or decline the application.


Admissions staff may consider how narrowly you missed, whether the result concerns a required subject, your overall performance, available capacity, and contextual information. Check the official portal before assuming the outcome. If necessary, contact admissions with your applicant ID, achieved total, HL grades, named-subject result, and document status.


RevisionDojo's guide to an[IB score below a university offer](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-score-below-university-offer) explains possible outcomes. Its article on[IB component scores in admissions](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/do-universities-consider-ib-component-scores) clarifies when detailed marks may matter after a narrow miss.


Do not request an Enquiry Upon Results automatically. Discuss component marks, grade boundaries, fees, risks, and deadlines with your coordinator, and ask whether the university will wait for the outcome.


### Common mistakes to avoid


- **Reading only the total:** HL and named-subject requirements can be decisive.
- **Confusing predictions with conditions:** Predictions support selection; final grades normally satisfy the offer.
- **Assuming extra points compensate:** A higher total does not automatically replace a missed subject grade.
- **Choosing a risky insurance offer:** Lower total points do not always mean safer conditions.
- **Ignoring additional requirements:** Language evidence, deposits, checks, and documents may remain outstanding.
- **Failing to arrange transcripts:** Official results must reach the correct destination.
- **Treating flexibility as guaranteed:** Plan to meet the written terms, not an assumed allowance.


For results-day preparation, see[what happens after an IB conditional offer](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-university-offer-depends-on-results) .


### Conclusion


Understanding conditional offers requires reading every condition literally. Your target may combine an overall Diploma score, HL profile, named subject grade, full Diploma status, language evidence, and administrative deadlines.


Build a balanced university list and preserve the exact wording of each offer. RevisionDojo's Questionbank, Study Notes, Mock Exams, and Jojo AI can support focused preparation, particularly in subjects named explicitly in your conditions.
